sources.entry: Ravenpass - Local-first password manager with native autofill, passkeys, and two-factor codes, with no account required.

summary.one_liner: Ravenpass is a local-first password manager that stores passwords, passkeys, two-factor codes and other items in an encrypted vault, with system autofill and no account required.
summary.what_it_does: Stores passwords, passkeys, two-factor codes, payment cards, identities with document scans, secure notes and crypto wallet seeds in one encrypted vault. Items are encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305 and unlocking is bound to device secure hardware such as the Secure Enclave or Android Keystore. Autofill works through the system's autofill on macOS and Android, and a Chrome extension talks to the desktop app over an end-to-end encrypted local connection. The vault can live on the device or in a cloud drive folder shared between computer and phone. It also generates passwords and passphrases, offers optional breach checks using only a 5-character hash prefix via Have I Been Pwned, imports from other password managers, and keeps deleted items in a trash for 30 days by default. Automatic encrypted backups and a 24-word recovery key are included.
use_cases: Store and autofill passwords across apps and browsers
Keep two-factor codes and passkeys in one vault
Sync an encrypted password vault between computer and phone via a cloud drive folder
Check whether saved passwords appear in known data breaches
Migrate passwords from another password manager
Store secure notes and crypto wallet seeds offline
notable: Local-first vault with no account; you choose where the vault file lives
Native system autofill on macOS and Android, plus a Chrome extension that fills payment cards
Passkey and two-factor code support alongside passwords
Breach checks send only the first five characters of each password hash
Encrypted automatic backups and a printable or savable 24-word recovery key
caveats: Described as in beta; the README advises keeping backups of stored items
macOS build needs Apple silicon and macOS 13+; AutoFill needs macOS 15; Android passkeys need Android 14
Windows, Linux and iOS are listed as coming soon; Chrome extension needs the desktop app running
Building from source requires several toolchains (Go, Node, Xcode, Android SDK/NDK)
